title: HexaBlock Suite level definition
description: One generic level schema with a payload specific to each gameId (FR-23, ADR-0004). The format is described in docs/level-format.md. JSON Schema checks the shape only; the rules that need geometry (connected figure, no holes, equal area) are checked by the level builder and the API's validator for each gameId.

formatVersion.description: Version of this format. A reader rejects a file whose formatVersion it does not know.

gameId.description: The variant that plays this level. Only level-based variants have level files.

levelId.description: Stable identifier: the gameId, a hyphen and the level number in three digits. It never changes, even when the level is edited.

number.description: Position of the level in its variant's progression, starting at 1. The next level is number + 1.

version.description: Edit counter of this level, starting at 1. It grows by 1 every time the level changes, so a client knows which levels to download again (FR-14).

difficulty.description: Designer's difficulty from 1 (easiest) to 5 (hardest), used to check that the progression is progressive (FR-46, FR-55).

payload.description: The section specific to the gameId. Its shape is chosen by the rules below.

coordinate.description: A cell coordinate as a list of integers. The topology says how many there are and what they mean; for "hex" it is [q, r] in axial coordinates.

board.description: The board of the level: a topology and a shape in that topology (ADR-0004, ADR-0006 in the client).

topology.description: The grid geometry. Only "hex" exists today (axial coordinates, 6 neighbors, 60 degree rotation). Another geometry is a new value here and a new topology in the client, never a new schema.

hexagonShape.description: A regular region of the topology around the origin. For "hex", radius 2 gives 19 cells (FR-50).

cellListShape.description: An arbitrary set of cells, listed one by one. Hexa Fit uses it for the figure (FR-40).

color.description: A tile color. The client maps each name to its palette and its glyph (UI mockups, D12).

pieces.description: The fixed set of pieces (FR-40, FIT-2). Each piece lists its cells relative to its own origin [0, 0], which is also the point it rotates around.

par.description: The two thresholds of FIT-3: one extra star for moves <= moves, one for whole seconds <= seconds.

solution.description: Optional proof that the level can be solved: one placement per piece, in the order of pieces. Tests use it; the game never shows it.

rotation.description: Rotation steps of the topology, applied before moving the piece's origin to "at".

goal.description: Number of blocks of 10 or more tiles to remove to win (FR-53, FR-54, SORT-4, SORT-5).

tray.description: Parameters of the seeded generator that draws the stacks of the tray (SORT-6, NFR-05).

seed.description: Seed of the random source. The same level always offers the same sequence of stacks.

stackSize.description: Number of tiles in each drawn stack, both ends included.

moveThresholds.description: The two thresholds of SORT-7, the larger first: one extra star for each threshold the moves are <= to.
